# Configuration reference

The configuration file is `$HERACLES_CONFIG` (or `--config PATH`). Every setting is
shown below with its comment, as in [`deploy/production/heracles.example.yaml`](../deploy/production/heracles.example.yaml); commented lines are optional settings
with their default or an example value.

Heracles configuration, fully commented. The setup wizard (or `heracles init`) writes a file like this one; write it by hand only if you prefer. Keep it readable by the Heracles user only: it holds the service account password. Nothing here is a real secret. Path: $HERACLES_CONFIG or `heracles serve --config PATH`.

## The directory

```yaml
directories:
  - id: main                        # short identifier, used in URLs and the audit log
    label: Main directory           # name shown in the console
    uri: ldaps://ldap.example.org   # ldap://, ldaps:// or ldapi://
    # starttls: true                # upgrade an ldap:// connection (not needed with ldaps://)
    # ca_file: /etc/ssl/certs/corp-ca.pem   # CA to trust when the server uses a private one
    bind_dn: cn=heracles,ou=services,dc=example,dc=org   # service account the console uses
    bind_password: CHANGE_ME        # or set HERACLES_DIRECTORY_MAIN_BIND_PASSWORD instead
    # bind_password_file: /run/secrets/bind_password   # read it from a file instead (Docker or
    #                                 # Kubernetes secrets); not together with bind_password
    base_dn: dc=example,dc=org
    # timeout: 10                   # seconds before an operation gives up
    # pool_size: 8                  # connections kept open to the server
```

## The console

```yaml
api:
  # Accounts that bypass the access rules (bootstrap administrators). Keep it short; delegate
  # everyday administration with roles instead.
  admin_dns:
    - uid=admin,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org

  # Host names the console may build links from (invitations, CAS). Set your public name.
  allowed_hosts: ["heracles.example.org"]

  # Reverse proxy in front of the console (TLS termination): the address the console sees it
  # connect from (in a container, the Docker network gateway, e.g. 172.16.0.0/12). Only a listed peer is
  # believed when it sends X-Forwarded-For / X-Forwarded-Proto, which the client address of the
  # login throttling, the audit log and the HSTS header rely on.
  # login:
  #   trusted_proxies: ["172.16.0.0/12"]

  session:
    cookie_secure: true             # false only when you serve plain http (trials)
    # idle_timeout_seconds: 1800
    # absolute_timeout_seconds: 28800

  # API tokens for scripts (Authorization: Bearer hrc_...), created by each person on their
  # account page. Every token expires; it acts as its owner, limited by its scope.
  # api_tokens:
  #   enabled: true
  #   max_lifetime_days: 365
  #   max_per_owner: 20

  # SCIM 2.0 provisioning at /scim/v2 (identity providers, HR systems). Off unless enabled
  # here. API tokens only: create a token with the write scope on the account page of the
  # provisioning account.
  # scim:
  #   enabled: true
  #   user_base: ""        # department DN for new users (default: the directory base)
  #   group_base: ""       # department DN for new groups
  #   max_results: 200     # largest page of a list request
  #   user_attributes:     # extra SCIM path -> LDAP attribute mappings (plain strings)
  #     "title": "description"

  # Sign-in through your identity provider (OpenID Connect, authorization code + PKCE). Off
  # unless enabled here; read from this file only. The password form stays available (and
  # audited) as the fallback. Register the redirect URI
  # <public_url>/api/v2/auth/oidc/callback and the post-logout URI <public_url>/login.
  # oidc:
  #   enabled: true
  #   issuer: https://login.example.org/realms/staff   # its discovery document must match
  #   client_id: heracles
  #   client_secret_file: /run/secrets/oidc_client_secret
  #   # client_auth: client_secret_basic   # or client_secret_post, or none (public client)
  #   # scopes: [openid, profile, email]
  #   # The claim naming the person must be one people cannot change at the provider (whoever
  #   # edits it picks the account): an immutable login, or email with email_verified.
  #   claim: preferred_username
  #   # attribute: uid                     # directory attribute it must equal (one entry)
  #   label: Example SSO                   # "Sign in with Example SSO" (default: generic text)
  #   # allowed_groups: [heracles-admins]  # only these values of groups_claim may sign in
  #   # groups_claim: groups
  #   # role_mapping:                      # value of groups_claim -> directory roles held for
  #   #   heracles-helpdesk:               # this session only (access rules; the directory
  #   #     - cn=helpdesk,ou=roles,dc=example,dc=org   # entry is not changed; one DN per
  #   #                                  # "- " line: a [..] list splits a DN at its commas)
  #   public_url: https://heracles.example.org
  #   # ca_cert_path: /etc/ssl/certs/internal-ca.pem

  # Built console to serve. The container image finds /app/static by itself.
  # static_dir: /app/static

  # Application database: sessions, login throttling, task reports, plugin switches.
  # Default: SQLite in $HERACLES_DATA_DIR/heracles.db.
  # database:
  #   path: /var/lib/heracles/heracles.db
  #   # Or PostgreSQL, to share state between replicas on several hosts:
  #   # url: postgresql://heracles:CHANGE_ME@postgres:5432/heracles

  # Largest request body in bytes (413 above), and the larger limit of the import endpoints.
  # max_body_bytes: 10485760
  # max_import_body_bytes: 33554432
```

## Plugins

```yaml
# Extensions that are on. Absent key: the core profile (posix, ssh, sudo, mail, audit,
# acl_admin, ppolicy). A plugin only works if the directory schema supports it. The console
# can switch plugins later; its choice is stored in the database and wins over this list.
plugins:
  enabled: [posix, ssh, sudo, mail, audit, acl_admin, ppolicy]
  # enabled: ["*"]                  # every plugin the schema supports
```

## Outgoing mail (password recovery, reminders, notifications)

```yaml
# Without a host, the tasks that send mail are skipped and reported as such.
# mail:
#   host: smtp.example.org
#   port: 587
#   sender: heracles@example.org
#   starttls: true
#   username: heracles
#   password: CHANGE_ME
#   # password_file: /run/secrets/smtp_password   # instead of password
```

## Access governance (plugin "access")

```yaml
# End dates on memberships, access requests and access reviews.
# access:
#   approvers: ["cn=access-approvers,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=org"]  # approve any request
#   requestable: "(owner=*)"     # groups and roles people may ask for
#   max_days: 365                # longest end date (0: permanent grants allowed)
#   remind_days: 7               # worker: mail a person this many days before a grant ends (0: off)
#   auto_close: true             # worker: close review campaigns once their deadline has passed
#   mail:                        # mail_template names; empty: built-in wording
#     request_submitted: ""
#     request_decided: ""
#     request_for_member: ""     # a request filed for someone else, mailed to that person
#     review_assigned: ""
#     grant_expiring: ""         # the reminder before an end date
```

## Audit

```yaml
# Retention of the audit log, chain anchors and forwarding to a log collector. Every event is
# hash-chained to the previous one; `heracles audit verify` checks the chain.
# audit:
#   retention:
#     days: 365                # purge events older than this (0: keep)
#     count: 0                 # keep at most this many events (0: no limit)
#   anchor_minutes: 60         # send the chain head to the collector this often
#   syslog:
#     address: "logs.example.org:6514"   # or a socket path such as /dev/log
#     transport: tls           # udp (default), tcp or tls
#     format: json             # text (default), json or cef
#     framing: octet-counting  # tcp/tls: octet-counting (default) or newline
#     facility: local0
#     ca_file: /etc/heracles/log-ca.pem  # tls: trusted authorities (default: the system ones)
#     # cert_file / key_file: client certificate, when the collector asks for one
```
